title: Chart tab silently coerces/drops non-finite series values while Statistics tab throws into the ErrorBoundary
description: toQuoteRow reads each series value with Number(row[col] ?? 0). The ?? only catches null/undefined, so a genuinely-null cell becomes a fabricated 0 plotted on the chart, and a non-numeric value (e.g. the string 'n/a') becomes NaN. The Chart render path then propagates NaN into SVG geometry with no user-facing signal, whereas the Statistics tab feeds the exact same rows to computeScenarioStatsBySeries, whose readFiniteNumber THROWS on null/empty/non-finite. The result: identical preview data renders a silently-wrong/broken chart in the Chart tab but trips the panel's ErrorBoundary (App.tsx:647, replacing the whole preview with the error fallback) the instant the user switches to the Statistics tab. This is an inconsistent, silent-wrongness path that contradicts the project's 'fail loudly, no incorrect fallbacks' guidance.
evidence: Line 50: vals[col] = Number(row[col] ?? 0)  // null -> 0 (silent fake value); 'abc' -> NaN. buildSeriesScale line 94: const v = r.values[column] ?? 0 (NaN ?? 0 === NaN, not caught) -> NaN never updates vMin/vMax. SeriesLine line 265: `...${yScale(r.values[column] ?? 0).toFixed(1)}` and lines 274-277 cx/cy=yScale(NaN) -> 'NaN' path segment + circle at NaN (invisible/broken) with no warning. Contrast optimiserScenarioStats.ts readFiniteNumber (line 31-38) which throws Error('Expected finite numeric value...') for the same null/'abc' cell; computeScenarioStatsBySeries is called from line 528-536 inside a useMemo, so the throw during render hits ErrorBoundary name="NodePreview" at App.tsx:647. Same data -> silent broken chart vs hard error fallback depending only on which tab is active.
